# beeps commands

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-cli-docs.mjs from the CLI itself; do not edit. -->

75 commands. Every one prints JSON on stdout; `beeps <command> --help` lists its options, and the skills explain when to use each.

## Top-level commands

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps capabilities` | print the patch schema, source types, archetypes, commands and error codes |
| `beeps init` | create .agent-beeps/ (project.json, patches/, kit.json, sets/, sessions/, taste/, renders/) |
| `beeps list` | list project patches |
| `beeps new` | validate a patch JSON file and save it to .agent-beeps/patches/<name>.json (to mirror a whole directory of committed patches, use sync) |
| `beeps sync` | mirror a directory of patch .json files (e.g. the ones your repo commits) into .agent-beeps/patches/: adds new names, replaces changed ones, validates every file before writing any; kit add, kit check and lint then take the names |
| `beeps batch` | apply create/set/remove/delete operations to project patches atomically |
| `beeps render` | render, loudness-trim and measure patches (names, set candidate names, or .json paths) |
| `beeps measure` | full measured features of one patch |
| `beeps look` | look image (waveform + spectrogram + features); several refs make a contact sheet |
| `beeps export` | write the loudness-trimmed WAV of a patch: stereo, full render length, unless --channels 1 or --trim-tail. Seed: --seed, else the seed recorded in the kit (only an audition ship records one; kit add does not), else 1 |
| `beeps archetypes` | list the SFX archetypes generate can sample |
| `beeps generate` | sample an archetype, render and measure, and keep a diverse, lint-clean candidate set |
| `beeps mutate` | breed variations of a patch toward directions (brighter, darker, punchier, softer, shorter, longer, less-harsh, more-character) |
| `beeps crossover` | blend two patches (structure from a) and save the result as a project patch |
| `beeps lint` | check patches against the cited craft rules (renders them to measure); exits 1 only when a patch has errors, warnings exit 0; notes (e.g. "kit-level rules run only in kit check") are informational |
| `beeps family` | emit N similar patches from one template patch plus a table of rows; {{param}} placeholders and /json/pointer columns override the template, optional seeded ranges and jitter; every row is validated (E_SCHEMA names the row and pointer); deterministic |
| `beeps serve` | start (or reuse) the LAN audition server; prints its URL |
| `beeps predict` | seal your prediction for a set before the owner auditions it |
| `beeps instruments` | list the bundled instrument patches songs can play by name |
| `beeps bundle` | collect the export sidecars (*.wav.json) under a directory into <dir>/index.json, the catalog the game player loads |
| `beeps compress` | re-encode an exported bundle (WAVs and *.wav.json sidecars) as Ogg Opus in <outDir>, verify frame counts, alignment and loop wraps, and write its index.json |
| `beeps loopcheck` | decode encoded audio (ogg, mp3, wav...) and report its frame count against the sidecar and how its loop wraps: click size, level step and seam metrics; --engines also decodes it in real browsers |
| `beeps build` | render, export, compress and bundle only the assets whose input hash differs from the lock (or whose outputs are missing or modified); writes the lock and index.json |
| `beeps verify` | check outputs against the lock (sha256, size), the catalog, and container headers (Opus granule length, MP3 Xing tag and encoder id); target: the output directory or a lock file (default: the build config) |
| `beeps analyze` | measure audio files beeps did not render (WAV directly; MP3, Ogg, FLAC... through ffmpeg): the patch features plus where the sound is, whether and how it repeats (onsets, rate, regularity, level between events, per-band decay of the mean event) and its spectrum shape. Needs no project |
| `beeps compare` | a candidate audio file against a reference: signed deltas (candidate minus reference) and hints on what to change. Export a patch or song first (beeps export / beeps song export), then compare the WAV |

## `set`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps set create` | render existing patches (names or .json paths) into a candidate set, so a hand-authored kit can be auditioned (use --flow explore) |

## `kit`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps kit list` | print the project kit: each sound with its family, priority and loudness trim |
| `beeps kit add` | render a patch, measure its loudness trim and add it to the project kit |
| `beeps kit remove` | take a sound out of the project kit (the patch file stays) |
| `beeps kit check` | render every kit sound and run patch and kit rules (one "no", priorities, families, key, masking) |

## `taste`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps taste show` | what the owner has preferred so far, in words and weights, with confidence |
| `beeps taste fit` | refit from the verdict logs and write model.json and summary.md |
| `beeps taste import` | log the thumbs from a listening page (a game's "click through every sound" export) as taste verdicts: liked beats disliked within a family |
| `beeps taste stats` | agent and model prediction hit rates |

## `audition`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps audition open` | open a comparison or exploration of a candidate set on the LAN page |
| `beeps audition formats` | blind-audition compressed delivery formats: encode WAV masters (a bundle directory, WAV files, --set or --album) through the compress presets next to a hidden lossless reference and a low-pass anchor, and serve the rating page |
| `beeps audition formats-status` | ratings so far for a delivery-format audition: per role, each preset against the hidden reference, listener screening and the smallest acceptable preset (no --id: list them) |
| `beeps audition wait` | block until the owner asks to refine, ships or abandons; prints that event |
| `beeps audition round` | answer a refine request with a new candidate set (it joins the audition against the champion) |
| `beeps audition status` | stage, champion, pending refine request and (after ship) the reveal |
| `beeps audition list` | sessions in this project |
| `beeps audition close` | abandon a session |
| `beeps audition stats` | how often agents and the taste model predicted the owner's pick |

## `instruments`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps instruments rebase` | print the song-instrument override that builds an instrument at another register, so a part written far from its root plays as built |

## `song`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps song new` | validate a song JSON file and save it to .agent-beeps/songs/<name>.json |
| `beeps song list` | project songs and bundled library songs |
| `beeps song check` | validate songs and print their outline (sections, notes and range per track) without rendering |
| `beeps song compat` | plan crossfades between songs without rendering: tempo, loop length, estimated key, and per pair the tempo relation, phase-lock and harmony agreement |
| `beeps song render` | render, loudness-trim, measure and lint songs; writes a WAV and a look image per song |
| `beeps song stems` | render each track alone at the full mix's trim: per-track level, brightness, low end and section presence, plus stem WAVs |
| `beeps song states` | adaptive songs: render the layers and judge every state as its own piece (level, trim, range, seam, brightness, register overlaps among only its tracks, lint) |
| `beeps song lint` | render (or reuse) a song and check it against craft/music-rules.json |
| `beeps song export` | write the loudness-trimmed WAV of a song |

## `album`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps album open` | print album links immediately, then add each song as its render finishes |
| `beeps album feedback` | the owner's marks, tags and notes per track |
| `beeps album list` | albums in this project |

## `player`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps player selftest` | write a static self-test page (beeps-selftest/) that decodes a known loop in the delivered formats through the vendored player and prints frame delta and lead per audio-context rate, with a copyable result: open it on a real iPhone or Safari |
| `beeps player export` | vendor the player into <dir>/beeps-player/, replacing that folder (import beeps-player/player/player.js) |

## `store`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps store push` | publish every locked asset whose outputs verify and that the store lacks (first writer wins; entries are never replaced) |
| `beeps store pull` | write the locked assets from the store into the output directory, verifying every file against the lock |
| `beeps store status` | per locked asset: are its outputs built here, and is it in the store |

## `ci`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps ci export` | write a zero-dependency fetch.mjs into <dir>: `node fetch.mjs` materialises the output directory from the store by hash and verifies sha256, with no beeps, Chromium or ffmpeg |

## `runtime`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps runtime export` | write <out>/<id>.runtime.json for each patch: the parsed patch, its seed, the project scale and the loudness trim the baked pipeline measures, which is what a game loads with parseCue (beeps build writes the same files) |
| `beeps runtime check` | lint the patch where the runtime path can take it: render each patch with every input at its default, at each end alone and with all inputs at min and at max, and run the craft rules on each. Findings the default does not have are the runtime path's own |
| `beeps runtime verify` | are the cues in <dir> current? Each cue's engine version, seed, scale and patch against the patch and the engine now, and its loudness trim against a fresh measurement (--no-trim skips the render). Exit 1 on any drift |
| `beeps runtime parity` | render every cue baked and through the runtime voice, in the same browser and seed, and report sample and feature differences against what each case owes (exact, near, bus, by-design), determinism over --runs fresh pages, and (with --engines) the other browsers against Chromium's bake. Exit 1 if a case misses its expectation |
| `beeps runtime perf` | time voice builds (first and warm) in Chromium and count the nodes and buffers they create; --vary-seed, --bus and --plays measure what a per-play seed, a shared reverb bus and a long session cost |
| `beeps runtime look` | look images of one cue at chosen inputs: the baked render (the patch with the inputs applied) and the runtime render, from the same seed. The image is the spectrogram and envelope the other look commands draw |
| `beeps runtime live` | move a live input mid-note and compare the running voice with static bakes of the two input values (Chromium; the patch must declare live bindings) |

## `sample`

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `beeps sample import` | retain exact original and canonical 48 kHz snapshot with provenance |
| `beeps sample prepare` | crop, linear fade and gain; seconds round to nearest 48 kHz frame; --recipe replays a saved frame recipe or receipt |
| `beeps sample overview` | image a recording of up to 120 s and list its natural segments (each at most ten seconds, with numbers and a ready prepare command); <source> is a sha256 sample ID or an audio file |
| `beeps sample bundle` | publish a portable source bundle; default includes only prepared dependencies |
| `beeps sample sync` | validate an entire source bundle, then add/update project patches and immutable dependencies |
